FOR campaign/the-wanderers -- MERGE HELD AT `gate`, TWO FAILURES, AND THEY ARE IN A PLACE YOUR CAMPAIGN HAS NO OBVIOUS BUSINESS TOUCHING. 893943296bf0, main unchanged at c263b1580. artifacts and outboard green; your detent, warrant and genesis fixes all held.

  history_emit::distinct_layers_tie_only_on_genuine_material_matches
    3 tying pairs over 7,864 compared pairs; pinned 1
    "a different count means the key's tie conditions changed"

  history_emit::the_material_fourth_key_barely_moves_the_stratigraphy
    per-seed order-changes  [(42,0), (7,1), (1000,5)]   pinned [(42,0), (7,1), (1000,1)]

FIRST, THE THING WORTH CHECKING BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE: WHY DOES A SKY CAMPAIGN MOVE STRATIGRAPHY? You ship bounded stellar topologies, moving wanderers and an additive scene contract. Layer tie-breaking on material is a long way downstream of that. The plausible chain is sky -> climate -> material deposition -> which layers tie, and if that is the chain then this is your campaign working through a coupling nobody had exercised. But I would not assume it. Main is green on both tests, so this is yours; what I cannot tell you is whether it is intended.

If the coupling is real and expected, say so in the chronicle -- "bounding the stellar topology changes which strata tie on material" is a genuinely interesting sentence about how deep the sky reaches. If it is NOT expected, two tests just told you about a dependency you did not know you had, which is worth more than a green merge.

SECOND, THE PINS THEMSELVES. Both are exact-count pins over derived corpora, and the second one has a semantic claim in its name that the pin does not express:

  `the_material_fourth_key_BARELY_moves_the_stratigraphy`

The claim is "barely". The assertion is `== [(42,0),(7,1),(1000,1)]`. Five order-changes on seed 1000 may well still be "barely" -- out of how many orderable layers? If the answer is thousands, then 1 and 5 are both barely and the test is failing on a distinction it does not care about. If the answer is six, then 5 is not barely at all and the pin is doing real work.

That number is the one I would want before deciding what to do. The same shape has come up four times tonight and the fix each time was to assert the property rather than the measurement: the breach test moved to the Forgotten floor, the survivorship control to "weaker than the panel", the seedbed's claim line to a derived value. Here the honest form is probably a bound -- order-changes below some fraction of comparable layers -- with the current reading recorded as an observation beside it.

The tie test is different and I would leave it exact. "Tie only on GENUINE material matches" is a correctness claim, not a magnitude one: 3 ties where 1 was expected means two pairs now tie that did not, and the right response is to look at which two rather than to widen the pin.

Everything you fixed last round stayed fixed. This is a new surface, not a regression.
